text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.0% today as oil prices climbed on escalating Middle East tensions. Iran has intensified attacks on Saudi Arabian facilities and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, stoking fears of supply disruptions that pushed global crude prices to $125.44 per barrel—a significant jump from the $96 range seen in U.S. markets. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly boost profit margins on barrels it sells.

The stock's broader two-week surge of 13.8% reflects a sustained rally as geopolitical risk has mounted. Diesel supply is now expected to remain constrained well into 2027 due to Iran-related disruptions and falling inventories, which reinforces the expectation of elevated energy prices for the foreseeable future—supporting valuations across upstream producers.
